claim: For a fluid Moon, the Roche limit is about 18,000 km from Earth's centre.
note: OWN INFERENCE (our calculation): fluid Roche limit = 2.44 R_Earth (rho_Earth/rho_Moon)^(1/3) = 18,365 km; densities from NASA fact sheets. Wikipedia's table lists ~18,381 km. Second source (found by search, page NOT read): SFU PHYS 390 lecture notes on tides and Roche limit https://www.sfu.ca/~boal/390lecs/390lec8.pdf (equal-density Roche limit ~2.456 Rp, disrupted material forms rings); Leinhardt et al., 'Tidal disruption of satellites and formation of narrow rings' https://arxiv.org/abs/1206.2677 (a rubble pile disrupts closer in than a fluid body; real result depends on the Moon's strength).
